stem: (Select TWO.) Dunmore Analytics' newest engineer is explaining a teammate's theories about what a `data` block can and cannot do, after one block's value showed as unresolved until the apply step. Which two of the following statements are correct?

choices.text: A data block can only perform read operations; it never creates or modifies a resource
A data block always creates a placeholder object in the state file that stays there until a `terraform destroy` clears it out
Terraform may defer a data block's read until the apply phase when its arguments depend on a resource being changed in the same plan
A data block appears in plan output as an add, change, or destroy action once Terraform reaches the apply step, the same as a resource block
Once a data block is first read, its value is locked and can never be refreshed on a later run

rationale: c misstates data blocks as managing a stateful placeholder object the way a resource does; a data block's presence in state records only what it read. d is wrong because data blocks never appear as add, change, or destroy -- at most as read. e is wrong because Terraform re-reads a data source on each run in the ordinary case; there is no permanent lock after the first read.
